messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Results with tip ranges shifted to the left by one.
parts:
This is probably due to having include_null_range=TRUE in the ML inference, but having include_null_range=FALSE in the plotting?  (The null range is always the first range in the ranges_list, if present). 

I ran the example script right now and it came out fine, so it may be that you changed something or have an old script.

Also -- make sure you're using the current version of BioGeoBEARS on GitHub, not an old version.

If none of that helps, please send me all scripts and input files.

Cheers!
Nick


On Tue, May 14, 2019 at 3:19 AM Grey Gustafson <gtgus...@gmail.com> wrote:
Greetings BioGeoBears group,

I am having an issue where my data is read in and displays correctly, but the results of the analysis have the tip range states shifted one to the left. Thus the first state no longer exists and is displayed as a black box throughout the tree while the rest of the tip ranges having been shifted one to the left. I get this issue if I run my rscript on the example Psychotria data as well.

Attached is the resultant file from the Pyschotria data (ignore the title it is for my actual data). 

As a note I get this result using both optimx and GenSA.

Thanks for your help!

Grey
